lectures.title: Making any Widget Tappable with InkWell

cues.en: So Let's now make sure
that these grid items are tappable.
And for that I'm going back to my category
grid item dart file and in there we can make this container
or any other widget tappable by wrapping this widget
that should be tappable with another widget
and that other widget would be the InkWell widget.
Now actually, the InkWell widget
is not just about making some child widget tappable
that could be achieved
with the GestureDetector widget as well.
If you wrap a widget like this container
with GestureDetector, you can add a broad variety
of listeners to it.
For example, onTap but also may other listeners
to listen all kinds of user interactions
with the child widget.
But if you use InkWell instead, you can also add
an onTap or many other listeners as you can see,
but in addition you get a nice visual feedback
if a user taps the item.
With GestureDetector you would get no feedback,
with InkWell you do, that's why I'm using InkWell.
With InkWell wrapped around container,
I can add the onTap parameter to set up a function
that will be triggered whenever this item will be tapped.
So with that, we already would be able to listen to events,
but I'm not done yet.
In addition, I'll set a splash color which will be important
for this visual tapping effect that we get.
And I'll set this to theme.of(context).primaryColor
to use one of my theme colors for that
or as a basis for this effect to be precise.
And we can also set a BorderRadius here
which does not want a number, but instead a BorderRadius
object which can be constructed in different ways.
For example, by using the circular constructor
which allows us to define a radius like 16
to give these items some nice rounded corners.
You can try out different values here
to get exactly the look you want.
So with that these items should be tappable.
Right now nothing happens when we tap them,
but they are tappable.
And if we saved this all and force a reload
we can see this effect in a very subtle way,
if you tap and hold one of these items,
you see they light up a little bit,
but of course we don't have the rounded corners
or at least we don't have the rounded corners
on these items right now.
If we tap one and hold this,
the highlighted fact indeed has rounded corners.
So the missing thing here indeed only is
to go to this container in our category grid item
and there in decoration, besides adding this gradient,
I also wanna add a BorderRadius
and just as on the InkWell this BorderRadius
should be set to BorderRadius circular 16, like this.
And with that, now we finally get these rounded corners
and this nice highlight effect if we tap and hold.
Of course, the next goal is to make sure
that we cannot just tap and hold,
but that we actually navigate to a different screen,
if we tap one of these items.
